title: Cyber Kill Chain
intro: A practical, command-first reference for the CPTS path, organised along the Lockheed Martin Cyber Kill Chain. Pick a stage to see the tools that matter there, or search by port, service or tool. Every entry is a working reference, not an exploit kit: use it only against systems you are authorised to test.

stages.name: Reconnaissance
stages.blurb: Map the target: hosts, open ports, services, versions, and the people and names around them. Passive OSINT first, then active scanning and enumeration.

stages.name: Weaponisation
stages.blurb: Turn a finding into something that will run on the target: a payload, a crafted document, a wordlist tuned to the environment.

stages.name: Delivery
stages.blurb: Get the payload or request to the target: a web request, an upload, a phishing email, a captured protocol.

stages.name: Exploitation
stages.blurb: Trigger the flaw and get first execution or access: a service exploit, a web vulnerability, a weak credential.

stages.name: Installation
stages.blurb: Make access durable and usable: a shell upgrade, a foothold, local privilege escalation, persistence.

stages.name: Command & Control
stages.blurb: Operate the foothold: a stable channel back to the operator, tasking, and tunnelling to reach deeper.

stages.name: Actions on Objectives
stages.blurb: Achieve the engagement goal: credential access, lateral movement, domain and data objectives, and the evidence for the report.
